The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Pnma (No. 62, Hall symbol −P 2ac 2n). The input cell is orthorhombic with lattice parameters a = 3.552236 Å, b = 5.961224 Å, and c = 6.830504 Å, all angles being exactly 90°. This input cell contains 12 atoms with composition V₄Co₄Si₄. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P is

P = [[0, 1, 0], [1, −1.6914683435228258×10⁻³⁴, 0], [−5.091546685144373×10⁻³³, −6.830012665051969×10⁻³³, −1.0000000000000002]]

and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). This matrix essentially interchanges the a and b axes and reverses the c axis, with negligible numerical noise on the order of 10⁻³³ in the off-diagonal terms, so the input cell can be recovered from the standard setting by applying this axis permutation and inversion.

All atoms occupy the threefold set of symmetry-equivalent positions generated by the 4c Wyckoff orbit, whose coordinate relation is (x, 1/4, z). Each element—vanadium, cobalt, and silicon—forms its own independent 4c sublattice, giving four atoms of each kind per cell, consistent with the declared composition. The representative positions, quoted to six decimal places as supplied (round_digits = 6), are as follows.

Vanadium occupies the 4c orbit with representative at (0.025034, 0.25, 0.822011); its independent parameters are x = 0.025034 and z = 0.822011, with y fixed at 1/4 by the site symmetry. Cobalt occupies a second, crystallographically distinct 4c orbit with representative at (0.142836, 0.25, 0.438966), so its independent parameters are x = 0.142836 and z = 0.438966, again with y = 1/4. Silicon occupies a third independent 4c orbit with representative at (0.266903, 0.25, 0.123841), giving x = 0.266903 and z = 0.123841 with y = 1/4.

Thus the three elements each lie on their own mirror-plane sublattice at y = 1/4 (and, by the Pnma symmetry operations, also at y = 3/4), stacked along the b axis. Within each mirror plane the V, Co, and Si atoms sit at progressively larger x coordinates (0.025034, 0.142836, and 0.266903 respectively) while their z coordinates span 0.822011, 0.438966, and 0.123841, so that the three species are offset from one another both along a and along c within the ac plane. The full 12-atom content of the cell is obtained by applying the four operations of each 4c orbit to these three representatives. No positional corrections beyond the stated six-decimal rounding were required; the listed coordinates represent the input geometry directly.
